How to use GRAAL

For readers who want to understand the question before the story, readers who want the story first, and teachers looking for a clear way to discuss AI, work and ownership.

Open GRAAL ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to graal-tau.vercel.app.

2

FR and EN at the top right switch the whole site; the choice is kept for the next visit.

3

Understand opens the explainer, The novel opens the book, Encyclopedia opens the glossary.

4

Try the experiment on the first screen jumps to the model; Discover the novel jumps to the book.

5

Nothing to install and no account: everything runs in the browser.

02

Features

01

The loop

A simplified economy of 100 goods. Move the share of work done by machines, choose what people receive besides wages, and set the share of the machines' value returned to people. Wages paid, money received and goods sold change as you move, and a status line says whether the loop still holds.

STEPS

  1. Move Share of work done by machines
  2. Pick Nothing, A basic income or A share of ownership
  3. Press The owners cut the payment and watch the loop
02

Income or ownership?

A calculator for a whole population: yearly profits from AI and automation, the share paid out to people, and the country or region. It gives what each person would receive in a year and in a month, and explains the difference between an income that can be switched off and a share that pays a dividend.

STEPS

  1. Set the yearly profits
  2. Set the share paid out
  3. Choose For whom and read the amount
03

The seven keys of real AI

A table of the resources every powerful AI depends on, what each one is and who controls it today. In the novel, each of these becomes a Key held by one dynasty.

STEPS

  1. Read the table row by row
  2. Compare who controls each resource
  3. Find the matching Key on the novel page
04

What a superintelligence could do

The paths researchers debate, from a single family holding all the power to the treacherous turn, the order taken literally, the arms race, machine war, collapse and the exit. Each one opens to a short explanation and says which of them the novel follows.

STEPS

  1. Open a scenario with the plus sign
  2. Read the explanation
  3. Close it and open the next
05

The world of the novel

The calendar counts from the Last Wage, in 2071. The page shows the Grail, the seven Keys with their Houses, words and seats, the people below, the main characters and the four books.

STEPS

  1. Open The novel
  2. Read the table of the seven Keys
  3. Scroll to the characters and the four books
06

Chapters as they are written

Book I lists every chapter of its first part with the point of view of each one. Published chapters are links; the others are waiting. The list grows as the book is written.

STEPS

  1. Scroll to Book I on the novel page
  2. Click a linked title
  3. Come back later for the next chapters
07

The reading page

Each chapter has its number, title, point of view, reading time and an epigraph from a source inside the world, then the text in a comfortable column. Previous and next links close the chapter.

STEPS

  1. Open a chapter
  2. Read the epigraph, then the text
  3. Use Next at the bottom to continue
08

The encyclopedia

127 entries in seven categories: characters, Houses, worlds, technology, society, history and words. Search ignores accents, chips filter by category with their counts, and nothing in it spoils the story.

STEPS

  1. Type a word in Search
  2. Tap a category chip
  3. Read the entry in English or French
03Tips
  • Read the explainer first if you want the question before the story; it takes about fifteen minutes.
  • Keep the encyclopedia open in a second tab while you read the chapters.
  • The models are teaching tools with their assumptions shown, not forecasts.
04FAQ
Is the novel finished?

No. Book I is being written and published chapter by chapter; four books are planned.

Is the novel in French?

Not yet. It is written in English first, and the French edition follows each book. The explainer and the encyclopedia are already in both languages.

Are real people or companies in the story?

No. The world, the families and the companies of the novel are invented.

Is the novel for adults?

Yes. It contains adult themes and coarse language.

Do I need an account?

No. Everything is free to read in the browser.
